records.heroLine: You don't stay here because it's luxurious. You stay because the building disappears into a landscape that feels older than anything you have walked through.
whyItMadeTheCut: Amangiri sits on more than 900 acres of the Colorado Plateau at Canyon Point, where the Entrada sandstone rises straight out of the desert floor. The architecture is concrete and glass, poured low into the rock so that the mesa, not the building, owns the view. There are 34 suites and, a short drive away, the ten tented pavilions of Camp Sarika. That is the whole place.

It made the cut for three reasons that cannot be built elsewhere. The setting: a privately held stretch of the Grand Staircase country, with slot canyons and a via ferrata on the property itself. The restraint: no lobby to speak of, no signage, a pool poured around a rock that was already there. And the access: Page's airstrip is a 25-minute drive, Lake Powell is at the door, and the great parks of the Southwest are a day trip in any direction.
It is not the most comfortable desert hotel in America. It is the one that lets the desert win.

jamesNote.text: There are hotels with views. Then there are places where the landscape is the hotel.

signals.line: 900 private acres of the Colorado Plateau, with the mesa as the only neighbour.
34 suites and ten pavilions, no through-traffic, no lobby crowd.
Concrete, glass and silence, poured around the rock rather than on top of it.
Page airstrip 25 minutes away; slot canyons and a via ferrata on the property.
There is no second Amangiri, and Aman is not building one.

records.worthAnotherNight: Yes, and not for the spa. The first two days go to the canyons and the pool. The third is when you stop moving, and the light on the mesa at six in the evening becomes the reason you came. Four nights is the right number; add a night at Camp Sarika if you can.
whoItMayNotSuit: Travellers wanting a large social resort
